key_insight: MECx accelerates discovery of low-energy ordered alloy configurations by steering Monte Carlo search with a bond-count-informed surrogate model instead of running DFT at every step.
engineering_relevance: This enables more practical prediction of ordering in multi-principal element alloys, helping design compositions with target local structure, thermodynamics, and potentially measurable diffraction signatures.
method: Train a surrogate energy model on 100 DFT-labeled configurations stratified by bond-count space.
Use the surrogate to guide Monte Carlo exploration of ternary, quaternary, and quinary BCC alloy configurational spaces.
Validate transferability on selected binary subsystems and compare ordered states against direct DFT-based Monte Carlo.
evidence_signal: Across ternary, quaternary, and quinary BCC alloys, the method found lower-energy ordered configurations than direct DFT-based Monte Carlo within practical limits, and the predicted states produced distinguishable superlattice reflections in simulated neutron diffraction.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and representativeness of the compact training set, so insufficient bond-space coverage could limit surrogate reliability in new alloy systems.
paper_title: Bond-informed search for ordered configurations in multi-principal element alloys
